sets.relationshipLabel: the thing that lets the action happen
sets.explanation: An oar is what makes rowing possible just as a flipper is what makes swimming possible — each is the enabling part without which the action can't occur.

sets.relationshipLabel: two names for the same thing (order-free)
sets.explanation: Selkie and seal-folk name the same mythical being, just as pelt and hide name the same animal covering — the pairing works in either order, which is the point of this one.

sets.relationshipLabel: near point : far point along a single axis
sets.explanation: Shoreline sits near and horizon far along the sea's breadth, just as surface sits near and seabed far along its depth — both pairs read shallow-to-deep, near-to-far.

sets.relationshipLabel: a place and the item hidden or stored there
sets.explanation: A chest conceals a stolen sealskin and a rafter conceals a hidden net — each pair names the hiding place and the very object the selkie tales turn on.
